newsitem.title: USA: Rubin hopes Fed candidates to be confirmed quickly.
newsitem.headline: Rubin hopes Fed candidates to be confirmed quickly.

text.p: Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said Monday two candidates to fill Federal Reserve Board governor vacancies were excellent choices and he hoped Congress would confirm them quickly.
"They're both excellent candidates. I don't know what the timetable will be, and I don't see any reason why they shouldn't move expeditiously," Rubin told reporters.

The White House has confirmed that Roger Ferguson of consulting firm McKinsey & Co Inc and Edward Gramlich, a University of Michigan economics professor, have been chosen to fill the two Fed positions.
Rubin spoke to reporters following remarks to an African business group, at which he urged the continent to pursue economic reform policies and said the United States would support these activities.
Clinton last week approved his staff's recommendations of Ferguson and Gramlich for the positions on the central bank's seven-member board and asked that they be sent for further background checks.

A U.S. official said Sunday that no problems have cropped up so far for either man in the vetting process, which he estimated would take two to three weeks after which Clinton may chose to make a formal nomination.

The Federal Reserve's two vacancies opened up earlier this year with the departure of Janet Yellen for the White House Council of Economic Advisers and Lawrence Lindsey for the conservative American Enterprise Institute think tank.

The vacancies came at a sensitive time for the central bank, which last month raised interest rates for the first time in over two years in an effort to head off inflation and keep the economy on track.

If nominated and confirmed by the Senate, Ferguson would be the third black to serve on the Federal Reserve board, following Emmett Rice, appointed by President Jimmy Carter, and Andrew Brimmer, named by President Lyndon Johnson.
